original_question: What is the image of the entropy map H: PD_n → SubMod_n given by H(Σ)_I = -log det(Σ_I) for each principal minor Σ_I of a positive definite symmetric matrix, how does that image intersect the faces of the submodular cone SubMod_n, and what are the fibers of H?
target_in_paper: Section 4, General Problem, as reformulated immediately after Proposition 4.4: to characterize the image of the entropy map H, how that image meets the faces of the submodular cone SubMod_n, and the fibers of H. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.4558))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official entropy-map formulation. It names the correct map H: PD_n → SubMod_n, uses the correct coordinate formula H(Σ)_I = -log det(Σ_I), and asks exactly about the three issues the paper singles out: the image of H, its intersections with faces of SubMod_n, and the fibers of H. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.4558))
missing_details: The paper works with real positive definite symmetric n×n matrices Σ, viewed as covariance matrices of mean-zero Gaussian random variables on R^n; that ambient real setting should be stated explicitly. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.4558))

SubMod_n should be defined explicitly as a cone in R^{2^n} with coordinates H_S for all subsets S ⊆ {1,2,…,n}, cut out by the inequalities H_{ {i}∪K } + H_{ {j}∪K } ≤ H_{ {i,j}∪K } + H_K for every K ⊆ {1,…,n} and i,j ∉ K. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.4558))
It should be made explicit that H uses the logarithms of all 2^n principal minors of Σ, with Σ_I denoting the principal minor indexed by I ⊆ {1,…,n}. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.4558))

For a fully paper-faithful stand-alone statement, one should include the bridge supplied by Proposition 4.4: Gaussian conditional independence models are precisely the inverse images under H of faces of SubMod_n, because equality in the determinant inequality (4.4) matches equality in the submodular inequality (4.3). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.4558))

The draft does not say that this is the section’s general problem, not the section’s specific problem. In the paper, the specific problem is the n=5 question asking which sets of almost-principal minors can vanish for a positive definite symmetric 5×5 matrix. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.4558))

No homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifiers occur in this problem; the only omitted quantifiers are the universal ones over all subsets K and all admissible i,j in the definition of SubMod_n. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.4558))
refined_question: For a fixed n, let PD_n be the cone of real positive definite symmetric n×n matrices, and let SubMod_n ⊂ R^{2^n} be the cone with coordinates H_S indexed by all subsets S ⊆ {1,2,…,n}, defined by the inequalities H_{ {i}∪K } + H_{ {j}∪K } ≤ H_{ {i,j}∪K } + H_K for every K ⊆ {1,…,n} and i,j ∉ K. For Σ ∈ PD_n, define H(Σ) by H(Σ)_I = -log det(Σ_I), where Σ_I is the principal minor indexed by I. Since Gaussian conditional independence models are exactly the inverse images under H of faces of SubMod_n, characterize the image H(PD_n), determine how H(PD_n) intersects the faces of SubMod_n, and describe the fibers of H. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.4558))
equivalent_formulation: Study the geometry of conditional independence models for multivariate Gaussian random variables. The paper explicitly says that the entropy-map question is a paraphrase of this general problem once Proposition 4.4 has identified Gaussian conditional independence models with inverse images of faces of SubMod_n under H. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.4558))
justification: The draft is not aiming at the section’s specific n=5 gaussoid-representability question; instead, it is already targeting the later, official reformulation of the section’s general problem in terms of the entropy map. That makes the nearest paper statement the Section 4 General Problem on page 10, read together with the immediately preceding definition of SubMod_n and H and Proposition 4.4, which explains why faces of SubMod_n are the relevant objects for Gaussian conditional independence models. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0707.4558))
